name: Bu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Bu/Jida-Abu (Nigeria): only Blench subclassification notes and wordlists; no phonological description located

new_statements.quote: 3.3 Tones The tone system of Bu has three level tones. No cases of glide tones seem to occur. [p. 2:] In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped and they will be added when time permits.
new_statements.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. The Bu language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 19 October 2011, 20 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. §3.3 Tones, p. 4 (PDF p. 6 of 20).
new_statements.locator: §3.3 Tones, p. 4 (printed page number); also §1 Introduction, p. 2 on tone marking
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (20 pp., PDF metadata 'Bu wordlist Unicode.doc', created 19 Oct 2011) and its text layer. The quoted passage is there exactly: '3.3 Tones / The tone system of Bu has three level tones. No cases of glide tones seem to occur.' on printed p. 4 = PDF page 5 of 20 (extracted text), not PDF p. 6 as the report said; the p. 2 sentence 'In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped and they will be added when time permits.' is also verbatim. I read the whole document: §3 Phonology (printed pp. 3-4) is explicitly 'based on rapid observations and should therefore be regarded as tentative'; it gives a 7-vowel + 3-nasal-vowel chart, a consonant chart and the two-sentence tone note…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only phonological description on record treats Bu as a three-level-tone language (H, M, L; no contour tones) and says nothing about word stress or accent; no stress placement rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author notes the /ə/ status is uncertain and that the phonology 'is based on rapid observations and should therefore be regarded as tentative' (p. 3).
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation-form wordlist elicited in one session (Nakere village, 8 Jan 1999); tones unmarked in the list; author calls the phonology 'tentative'. No statement about word-level prominence, stress or accent at all.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog buuu1244 'Bu' = the Bu (Abu) half of Blench's Bu-Ningkada cluster (Atlas ed. 3 entry 54: 54.a Bu, 54.b Ningkada; dialects Jida, Abu, Raga). Blench 2011's data are from the Bu (Abu) variety at Nakere village; the Ningkada (Jidda) variety, which Blench considers the same language with minor lexical/phonological differences, is not described separately. Not to be confused with the Chadic 'Bu (Zaranda)' [zbu] created in the same ISO 2020-031 cycle.
